provenance.passcode_note: PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL: the passcode the pinned `clienting.test.ts` publishes; it has never protected anything
provenance.agent_seed_note: PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL: the agent's seed is the fixed array in this generator, as Roadmap 5.5's fixture used
provenance.note: the clock is pinned as Roadmap 5.5's fixture pinned it, so the signed requests reproduce byte for byte including their signatures; the agent's key is fixed so its response signatures do too

declarations.passcode_length_check: if (bran.length < 21) { throw Error('bran must be 21 characters'); }
declarations.boot_body: data = { icp: evt.sad, sig: sign.qb64, stem: this.controller?.stem, pidx: 1, tier: this.controller?.tier, }
declarations.connect_anchor_check: if (this.agent.anchor != this.controller.pre) { throw Error( 'commitment to controller AID missing in agent inception event' ); }
declarations.random_passcode: export function randomPasscode(): string { const raw = libsodium.randombytes_buf(16); const salter = new Salter({ raw: raw }); // https://github.com/WebOfTrust/signify-ts/issues/242 return salter.qb64.substring(2, 23); }
declarations.random_nonce: export function randomNonce(): string { const seed = libsodium.randombytes_buf(libsodium.crypto_sign_SEEDBYTES); const seedqb64 = new Matter({ raw: seed, code: MtrDex.Ed25519_Seed }); return seedqb64.qb64; }

notes.boot: boot posts the controller's inception event, its signature, the derivation stem, a hardcoded `pidx: 1`, and the tier — to the *boot* URL, unauthenticated, because no agent exists yet to authenticate to
notes.connect: connect reads the agent state, rebuilds the controller against the returned establishment event, refuses an agent whose inception does not anchor this controller, approves the delegation when the controller is still at sequence zero, and only then builds the key manager and the authenticator
notes.fetch: the signed pipeline is Roadmap 5.5's; what the client adds is the controller prefix it stamps and the agent key it verifies against

connected.note: after connect the controller has advanced to the interaction event approving the delegation, and its anchor names the agent

pinned_confirmations.note: the controller prefix and the exact boot body are looked for among the literals the pinned `clienting.test.ts` asserts; the inception event is recorded beside them

random_shapes.passcode_note: `randomPasscode` builds a `Salter` from 16 random bytes and slices `qb64.substring(2, 23)` — dropping the two-character derivation code and taking 21 of the 22 remaining characters, which is the length the constructor requires
random_shapes.nonce_note: `randomNonce` is 32 random bytes under the Ed25519 seed code, qualified

boot_hardcodes_pidx_one.expression: data = { icp: evt.sad, sig: sign.qb64, stem: this.controller?.stem, pidx: 1, tier: this.controller?.tier, }
boot_hardcodes_pidx_one.note: the client's own `pidx` is zero at boot, but the body hardcodes `pidx: 1`; the two are never reconciled and nothing reads the field back
boot_hardcodes_pidx_one.rust_decision: reproduced verbatim, because the value is what a KERIA agent receives; it is a constant here rather than a field, so the two cannot disagree

approve_delegation_is_unauthenticated.note: the PUT that anchors the agent's delegation carries no HTTP signature at all — it bypasses `fetch` and calls the global directly, which Roadmap 5.1 also recorded
approve_delegation_is_unauthenticated.rust_decision: reproduced: the call is made on the unsigned transport, and the API says so. Changing it would produce a request KERIA does not expect.

passcode_save_and_delete_are_unauthentic.note: `saveOldPasscode` and `deletePasscode` also bypass `fetch`, so a passcode is written to the agent over an unsigned request
passcode_save_and_delete_are_unauthentic.rust_decision: reproduced, and named: both methods are documented as unauthenticated so a caller cannot mistake them for signed calls.

state_reports_404_as_a_message.expression: if (res.status == 404) { throw new Error(`agent does not exist for controller ${caid}`); }
state_reports_404_as_a_message.note: a missing agent is reported as a thrown string naming the controller; every other status falls through and is parsed as if it were the state
state_reports_404_as_a_message.rust_decision: typed: a 404 is `ClientError::AgentNotFound` and any other non-success status is `ClientError::Status`, so a 500 is never parsed as state.

connect_assigns_ridx_without_rederiving.note: connect assigns `controller.ridx` after construction without re-deriving any key, so the field and the keys it names can disagree
connect_assigns_ridx_without_rederiving.rust_decision: unrepresentable: Roadmap 4.5 fixes the rotation index at construction, so the controller is rebuilt with the returned index rather than mutated after the fact.

ready_is_libsodium_initialization.note: `src/ready.ts` is four lines that await libsodium's WebAssembly initialization; there is nothing protocol-level in it. The scan counts where the module is imported from, which is the export surface alone
ready_is_libsodium_initialization.rust_decision: `N/A`: the Rust cryptographic stack needs no asynchronous initialization, so there is nothing to port. Recorded against the file's own text.

fetch_requires_connect_at_run_time.expression: throw new Error('client need to call connect first');
fetch_requires_connect_at_run_time.note: `fetch` throws `client need to call connect first` when the authenticator is still null, which is a run-time check on a state the type system could have carried
fetch_requires_connect_at_run_time.rust_decision: unrepresentable: connecting consumes the unconnected client and returns a connected one, so there is no `fetch` to call before connecting.
